evidence.quote: In scenario-based design, descriptions of how people accomplish tasks are a primary working design representation.
Such descriptions, often called scenarios, support reasoning about situations of use, even before those situations are actually created.
Every scenario involves at least one agent and at least one goal.
Particular actions and events can facilitate, obstruct, or be irrelevant to given goals.
They are widely used for planning and describing evaluation test tasks (Roberts and Moran 1983)
a particular usage experience that could be prototyped and tested. At the same time,
in the sense that they are deliberately incomplete and easily revised or elaborated.
They describe systems in terms of the work that people will try to do as they make use of those systems.
All stakeholders speak the language of scenarios. Thus, employing scenarios as a focal design representation facilitates participatory design
And they describe designs at multiple levels of detail and with respect to multiple perspectives.
Each of these variations in resolution and perspective is a permutation of a single underlying use scenario.
